title: Reliability workbench notes - weekly ops prep
content:
Context / purpose:
- Prep for weekly SRE ops sync (handoff -> priorities -> action items). Want to go in with clear asks, quick data, and 3 prioritization buckets (Urgent, Next sprint, Observability backlog).
- Audience: SRE + oncall rotation + one rep from serving-runtime and platform-engineering.

Top bullets to cover (5-7m each):
1) SLO health snapshot (current week + trend)
   - Overall service availability: 99.92% (monthly rolling), target 99.95% -> error budget ~0.03% left (~2.6 hours/month).
   - P95 latency: 220ms (steady), P99 latency: 1.8s (spike on 6/04)
   - Error rate (5xx): baseline 0.08%, spike to 0.6% during 6/04 incident
   - Observed correlation: p99 spikes correlate with KV cache churn and long GC pauses on leader nodes.
   - Quick ask: prioritize 2-weeks mitigation to protect error budget.

2) Paging trends (last 30 days)
   - Weekly pager count: 18 -> 25 -> 31 (uptrend).
   - Top alert sources: high latency alerts (45%), infra autoscaler flaps (30%), model-load failures (15%), other (10%).
   - Note: Latency alerts often triggered by combined small increases across many pods; single-pod flaps rarely the cause.

3) Hot incidents recap (last 2 weeks) - short, action-focused
   - INC-4212 (6/04) - p99 latency burst & intermittent 5xx
     * Symptoms: 10-12 minute window of elevated p99 with cascading retries from clients. Root cause hypothesis: unexpected behavior in KV cache eviction algorithm under mixture of short/long sequences -> cache thrashing + memory pressure on serving nodes.
     * Mitigation applied: temporary increase in cache size (canary) and fallback routing to smaller model (t=0.8) for high-latency tenants.
     * Next: revert provisional change when a config with probing is ready. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-06-14.
   - OP-1337 (6/07) - autoscaler oscillation on dedicated pool
     * Symptoms: thrashing between scale up/down for GPU pool during traffic ramp. Likely because HPA config uses pod_cpu metric which is noisy for idle-warm pods.
     * Temporary fix: tighten scale down window to 5m, disabled burst scaling from test runners.
     * Long-term: switch to qps-based autoscaling (metric: requests_per_minute) + smoothing. Owner: Jordan. Due: 2026-06-21.

4) Quick metrics to surface in sync (graphs to pull)
   - Rolling 7d p99 / p95 latency by model family (gptx*, redwood-*/open variants)
   - Error-rate heatmap by region and model (us-west1, eu-west1)
   - Pager origin breakdown (alert rule name -> incident count)
   - KV cache eviction rate + memory usage vs latency (last 48h)

5) Proposed immediate action items (short list for decision):
   - A: Stabilize cache behavior: enable 2-stage eviction probe on canary (Samir) - low risk, roll now.
   - B: Tune alert thresholds: add a staging-only alert that excludes A/B test noise; lower sensitivity for p99 for heavy-batch jobs (Jordan / monitoring) - medium priority.
   - C: Synthetic steady-state test: add 30m synthetic test that simulates mixed short/long prompts, measure cache churn (Priya) - schedule this week.

6) Longer-term items (backlog/prioritization)
   - Rework autoscaler to use qps-based metrics + burst policy.
   - Add cost-aware fallback routing to avoid sending large-batch requests to high-cost GPU pools during pressure.
   - Model-loading circuit breaker: prevent retry storms during partial failures.

Notes to self / meeting scripts (useful lines):
- "We have ~2.6 hours/month of error budget left — objective is avoid burning that in the next 72 hours."
- "Immediate ask to platform: approve canary cache probe in us-west1 for 24h so we can validate GC/eviction effects."
- "If we see >2% new pager rate from latency alerts after config change, rollback and escalate."

Open questions / things to check before the sync:
- Is there a pending infra rollout that could interact with autoscaler? (check release-engineering calendar)
- Are there recent PRs that changed cache eviction config? (quick grep: serving-runtime PRs since 5/30)
- Can we get a smoke synthetic routing test in <12h? If not, plan for guarded canary.

Draft agenda (30m total):
- 0-5m: Quick health snapshot + error budget callout (me)
- 5-15m: Incident highlights & proposed mitigations (Samir/Jordan)
- 15-22m: Decide immediate actions (A/B/C) + owners
- 22-27m: Ops blockers / resource asks (tickets, infra windows)
- 27-30m: Quick round: blockers for next oncall rotation

Action tracker (quick):
- [ ] Samir: deploy 2-stage eviction probe to canary (us-west1) and monitor 48h. Due 2026-06-14. Linked: JIRA-INC-4212
- [ ] Jordan: prototype qps-based autoscaler in staging; propose rollout plan. Due 2026-06-21. Linked: JIRA-OP-1337
- [ ] Priya: create 30m synthetic mixed-workload test and add to cron (run every 6h for next 3 days). Due 2026-06-12.
- [ ] Elena (me): pull graphs + assemble 1-slide summary for sync (include error budget, last incident snapshot). Due 2026-06-10 (before meeting).

Retro notes (light):
- We are seeing more medium-severity pages that linger and cause cognitive load (many small pages are worse than one big page). Consider bundling thresholds or 'escalation grouping' for similar symptoms.
- Oncall fatigue: ensure rotation favors short, high-context handoffs and reduce noise from experiments.

Quick references / anchors to link in the meeting doc:
- Postmortem INC-4212 draft: confluence://reliability/postmortem-2026-06-04 (draft)
- Autoscaler discussion: https://go/release-engineering/autoscaler-notes (internal link stub)
- Serving-runtime PR that alters cache: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987

Random quick thoughts / scratch lines:
- If eviction probe shows no change, next is to add conservative prewarming for long-sequence tenants.
- Might be worth running a canary with smaller model perf profile to see if latency is model-specific or infra-general.
- Ask product for user-facing communication only if we exceed 1% error budget burn in a week.

-- end scratch --
